name: finch-image-gen
description: Generate and edit images with OpenAI GPT Image 2.5 (or an OpenAI-compatible relay): text-to-image, image-to-image, masked edits, transparent backgrounds and custom sizes, right inside Finch.

scripts.prepublishOnly: npm run typecheck && npm run build && npx @finchtoys/minitools doctor .

finch.name: Image Gen (OpenAI)
finch.description: Generate and edit images with OpenAI GPT Image 2.5 (or an OpenAI-compatible relay), with a masonry gallery you can re-edit from: text-to-image, image-to-image, masked edits, transparent backgrounds and custom sizes.
finch.systemPrompt: Use image_gen_create to generate images with OpenAI's image API. Text-to-image: pass only prompt. Image-to-image / reference-guided editing: also pass reference_image_paths (local absolute file paths); add mask_path to limit the edit to a masked area. COST POLICY: unless the user explicitly asks for something better, keep the cheap defaults — model gpt-image-2.5-flare, quality low, size 1024x1024. Do not upgrade quality or resolution on your own initiative; quality goes low → medium → high → xhigh → max and both quality and size drive cost and waiting time. Only switch to gpt-image-2.5-sunburst when precise editing matters, and say why when you do. size takes 'auto' or WIDTHxHEIGHT (1024x1024, 1536x1024, 1024x1536, 2048x2048, 2560x1440, 3840x2160 …). Set background='transparent' (with png or webp) when the user needs a cut-out. For a long, high-quality single render, pass partial_images 1-3 so progress stays visible. Generated images are saved locally as absolute file paths in the tool result and are also collected in the Image Gen gallery (left sidebar App View, or the Image Gen panel inside a session) — tell the user that when they ask where their pictures went; do not re-download or re-encode them, and use wechat_send or Session attach to show or share them. When the user attaches an image annotation or a boxed image region from that gallery, treat the attached file as the thing to edit: pass its path in reference_image_paths and apply the requested changes, honouring each box as the area to change. If the tool reports the OpenAI API key is missing, tell the user to click the Image Gen settings button (gear icon) in the Composer toolbar and choose "OpenAI API Key" to paste it in directly — no need to hunt through Toolcase. The same settings button also sets the default model, the default quality, and the "API Base URL" for a proxy/relay endpoint instead of api.openai.com (or pass base_url on a single image_gen_create call for a one-off override). When a request is blocked or rejected, the tool returns the API error code and a remediation hint — follow the hint instead of retrying the identical request.

appView.description: Browse every image you generated, with the model, quality and size it was made with.
